sourceHtml:
Anthropic is removing the five-hour limit from its Claude Max 20x plan, now renamed Ultra, for verified accounts. In a post on Claude’s X account at 1:29 p.m. Eastern on October 30, 2026, the company said the removal starts “today with most existing subscribers.” Max 5x becomes Max, still $100 a month, and Ultra stays at $200. Weekly limits aren’t changing, and the $100 Max plan keeps its five-hour limit.

Subscribers see both caps as bars under Settings > Usage: one for the current session, which resets every five hours, and one for the week. Our comparison of Claude subscription plans covers the other differences between Pro, Max and Team, using the plans’ old names.

Two new names, same prices

“If you’re a subscriber, there’s nothing you need to do,” Anthropic said in the post. Claude’s pricing page, as displayed in France on October 30, lists Max at €90 and Ultra at €180 a month, before tax.

Anthropic’s help center updated its Ultra page the same day, at 1:11 p.m. Eastern. According to that page, Max 20x subscribers move to Ultra automatically, with no price change, and the plan is available only as a monthly subscription. The email Anthropic sent Ultra subscribers on October 30, seen by maccus.fr, confirms that their “price, features, billing date, and weekly usage limit stay the same.”

For now, the rename is skin-deep: on the pricing page, the Ultra signup link still carries the “max_20x” identifier. Both plans also include a monthly API credit, $100 on Max and $200 on Ultra, which can’t be used in Claude Code or the Claude apps.

The rename doesn’t touch the invisible text watermark Claude puts on its output, which Anthropic extends to Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6 and Mythos 5 on November 3.

A limit lifted in stages, account by account

Anthropic explained the move in its email to Ultra subscribers: “More of Claude’s work now runs for hours in the background, and a 5-hour limit shouldn’t stop it partway.” Once the limit is removed, “you can spread your weekly usage limit across the week however you like,” the email says.

The removal is happening “in stages,” and only for verified accounts. According to the help center, Anthropic verifies Ultra accounts automatically “using factors like your account and payment history,” to help prevent fraud and abuse. Newer accounts keep a temporary limit until they’re verified, the X post says, and Anthropic emails subscribers once it’s lifted. Verifying a phone number at checkout is a separate step and doesn’t remove that limit.

The help center describes how to check: if the “Current session” bar no longer shows up under Settings > Usage, the account is verified.

Claude Code follows the same rule. Anthropic’s help page for the tool says Pro and Max plans have a five-hour session limit and a weekly limit, while verified Ultra accounts have only a weekly limit. That means the wrap-up allowance, which lets Claude Code finish the step in progress when a user reaches the five-hour limit, no longer applies to those accounts. On an Ultra account under the temporary limit, the allowance works as it does on Max.

Weekly limits are unchanged

Ultra’s weekly allowance stays at 10 times Pro’s usage, across all models, according to the pricing page and the help center. Max keeps 5 times Pro’s usage, every five hours and every week. Usage across Claude’s web, desktop and mobile apps, plus Claude Code, still draws from one shared pool, which our guide to hitting the usage limit on Claude Pro explains. The announcement covers only the two Max plans and leaves Free, Pro, Team and Enterprise untouched.

Fable models remain under a separate cap. On both Max and Ultra, they can use up to half the weekly limit, a rule already covered in our article on Claude models and their pricing. API usage is billed separately, at API rates.

The help center also carries a broader caveat: “Additional usage limits may apply to manage capacity and ensure fair access to all users.” Its examples include weekly or monthly caps and limits on model or feature usage, set at Anthropic’s discretion. The page adds that Anthropic doesn’t guarantee uninterrupted service.

The “20x” only ever applied to the 5-hour window

The email gives the reason for the name change. The company first introduced Max 20x as a way for Pro subscribers to upgrade to a five-hour limit 20 times higher. In August 2025, it added a weekly usage limit, set at 10 times Pro’s. The plan is getting a new name now because the 20x referred to the five-hour limit, which Anthropic is removing.

Mike Overell, who leads product for Claude subscriptions, laid out the timeline on X two minutes after the announcement. When the plan launched in April 2025, it had only a five-hour limit, set at 20 times Pro’s. Weekly limits came later, at 10 times Pro’s, while the five-hour limit stayed at 20 times.

“I get that some new users assumed 20x applied to both limits. We could have done better here, and I’m sorry,” he wrote. Replies to his post expressed surprise that the weekly limit had only been 10 times Pro’s, and one asked how users would be compensated.

On September 8, The Verge reported that an expanded class action accuses Anthropic of deceptively advertising the limits of its Max plan. The suit was brought by Monica Vaca and Kati Daffan, two attorneys who formerly worked at the Federal Trade Commission. In a motion to dismiss the earlier version of the complaint, Anthropic argued that details on those limits were available through links in the purchase process, the outlet reported. Neither the October 30 announcement nor the email mentions the case.

The questions the announcement leaves open

Anthropic hasn’t given a timeline for the staged rollout. The company says it is starting “with most existing subscribers,” but doesn’t say how many accounts remain under the temporary limit or how long it takes to verify a newer account.

The weekly limit is still expressed only as a multiple of Pro’s usage, with no message count. The pricing page notes that how fast a subscriber reaches a limit depends on the model used, the length of conversations and the size of files. None of the Anthropic pages cited here says when or how the additional capacity limits would apply.

What it means

On a verified Ultra account, the weekly limits now do all the rationing, aside from any capacity limits Anthropic reserves the right to impose. A subscriber can pack a week’s usage into a few long days, or let an agent or a Claude Code session run for several hours without being blocked by a session limit. Subscribers who were already hitting the weekly limit before the week was out gain nothing, since that cap hasn’t moved.

The gap between the two plans changes shape, too. For twice the price, Ultra gives twice Max’s weekly usage and, once the account is verified, has no five-hour cap. Max, like Pro, keeps its five-hour cap.

The rename fixes a label that Anthropic itself admits was misunderstood, while a class action targets how those same limits were presented. The next things to watch are how quickly the removal emails go out, what the capacity limits look like in practice and where the class action goes.

translation.html:
Anthropic 正在为已验证账户取消 Claude Max 20x 套餐的五小时用量限制，该套餐现已更名为 Ultra。公司于美国东部时间 2026 年 10 月 30 日下午 1:29 在 Claude 的 X 账户上发文称，将“从今天开始，先为大多数现有订阅用户”取消这一限制。Max 5x 更名为 Max，价格仍为每月 100 美元，Ultra 则维持每月 200 美元。每周用量限制不变，100 美元的 Max 套餐仍保留五小时用量限制。

订阅用户可以在“设置 > 用量”中看到这两项上限对应的进度条：一条显示当前会话用量，每五小时重置一次；另一条显示每周用量。我们的Claude 订阅套餐对比使用套餐的旧名称，介绍了 Pro、Max 和 Team 之间的其他区别。

两个新名称，价格不变

Anthropic 在帖子中表示：“如果你已经订阅，无需进行任何操作。”10 月 30 日在法国显示的 Claude 定价页面列出，Max 每月 90 欧元，Ultra 每月 180 欧元，均为税前价格。

Anthropic 帮助中心于同一天美国东部时间下午 1:11 更新了 Ultra 页面。该页面称，Max 20x 订阅用户将自动转为 Ultra，价格不变，且该套餐仅提供按月订阅。maccus.fr 查阅了 Anthropic 于 10 月 30 日发给 Ultra 订阅用户的邮件，其中确认，他们的“价格、功能、账单日期和每周用量限制保持不变”。

目前，更名只是表面变化：定价页面上的 Ultra 注册链接仍带有“max_20x”标识符。两个套餐还都包含每月 API 额度，Max 为 100 美元，Ultra 为 200 美元，这些额度不能用于 Claude Code 或 Claude 应用。

此次更名不影响Claude 在输出中添加的不可见文本水印，Anthropic 将于 11 月 3 日把这项水印扩展至 Opus 4.7、Opus 4.6、Sonnet 4.6 和 Mythos 5。

分阶段、逐账户取消限制

Anthropic 在发给 Ultra 订阅用户的邮件中解释了此举：“如今，Claude 的更多工作会在后台持续运行数小时，五小时限制不应该让它中途停下。”邮件称，取消这一限制后，“你可以按照自己的意愿，在一周内自由分配每周用量额度”。

取消限制正在“分阶段”进行，且仅适用于已验证账户。帮助中心称，Anthropic 会“根据账户和付款历史等因素”自动验证 Ultra 账户，以帮助防范欺诈和滥用。X 上的帖子称，较新的账户在完成验证前仍受临时限制，Anthropic 会在限制取消后向订阅用户发送邮件。在结账时验证手机号码是一个独立步骤，不会取消这项限制。

帮助中心说明了检查方法：如果“设置 > 用量”中不再显示“当前会话”进度条，就表示账户已通过验证。

Claude Code 遵循同样的规则。Anthropic 关于该工具的帮助页面称，Pro 和 Max 套餐设有五小时会话用量限制和每周用量限制，已验证的 Ultra 账户则只有每周用量限制。这意味着，允许 Claude Code 在用户达到五小时用量上限后完成当前步骤的收尾额度，不再适用于这些账户。对于仍受临时限制的 Ultra 账户，收尾额度的运作方式与 Max 相同。

每周用量限制保持不变

定价页面和帮助中心显示，Ultra 在所有模型上的每周用量额度仍为 Pro 的 10 倍。Max 在每五小时和每周两个周期内的用量额度均保持为 Pro 的 5 倍。Claude 网页版、桌面版、移动应用以及 Claude Code 的用量仍共用一个额度池，我们的Claude Pro 达到用量上限指南对此作了解释。此次公告仅涉及两个 Max 套餐，Free、Pro、Team 和 Enterprise 均不受影响。

Fable 模型仍受单独的上限约束。在 Max 和 Ultra 套餐中，这些模型最多可使用每周用量额度的一半，我们关于Claude 模型及其定价的文章已介绍过这一规则。API 用量按 API 费率单独计费。

帮助中心还附有一项范围更广的说明：“为管理容量并确保所有用户都能公平使用，可能会实施额外的用量限制。”列举的例子包括每周或每月上限，以及由 Anthropic 自行决定的模型或功能使用限制。页面还补充称，Anthropic 不保证服务不中断。

“20x”从来只适用于五小时窗口

邮件解释了更名的原因。公司最初推出 Max 20x，是为了让 Pro 订阅用户可以升级到五小时用量上限为原来 20 倍的套餐。2025 年 8 月，公司新增了每周用量限制，额度设为 Pro 的 10 倍。如今该套餐更名，是因为 20x 指的是 Anthropic 正在取消的五小时用量限制。

负责 Claude 订阅产品的 Mike Overell 在公告发布两分钟后，于 X 上梳理了时间线。该套餐于 2025 年 4 月推出时，只有五小时用量限制，额度设为 Pro 的 20 倍。后来增加了每周用量限制，额度为 Pro 的 10 倍，而五小时用量额度仍为 Pro 的 20 倍。

他写道：“我理解，一些新用户以为 20x 适用于两项限制。我们在这方面本可以做得更好，对此我很抱歉。”帖子的回复中，有人对每周用量上限一直只有 Pro 的 10 倍表示惊讶，还有人询问将如何补偿用户。

9 月 8 日，The Verge 报道称，一起扩大了诉讼范围的集体诉讼指控 Anthropic 对其 Max 套餐的用量限制进行了误导性宣传。该诉讼由 Monica Vaca 和 Kati Daffan 提起，两人都是曾在美国联邦贸易委员会任职的律师。据该媒体报道，Anthropic 在请求驳回早期版本诉状的动议中辩称，购买流程中的链接提供了这些限制的详细信息。10 月 30 日的公告和邮件均未提及此案。

公告留下的未解问题

Anthropic 尚未公布分阶段推出的时间表。公司称会从“大多数现有订阅用户”开始，但没有说明还有多少账户仍受临时限制，也没有说明验证一个较新账户需要多长时间。

每周用量上限仍仅以 Pro 用量的倍数表示，没有给出消息条数。定价页面指出，订阅用户达到上限的速度取决于所用模型、对话长度和文件大小。本文引用的 Anthropic 页面均未说明额外的容量限制会在何时、以何种方式实施。

这意味着什么

对于已验证的 Ultra 账户，除 Anthropic 保留权利实施的容量限制外，如今用量完全由每周上限控制。订阅用户可以将一周的用量集中在几天内长时间使用，也可以让智能体或 Claude Code 会话连续运行数小时，而不会被会话用量限制阻断。此前就会在一周结束前耗尽每周额度的订阅用户不会因此受益，因为这一上限没有变化。

两个套餐之间的差异也发生了变化。Ultra 的价格是 Max 的两倍，每周用量额度也是 Max 的两倍，而且账户一经验证，就不再有五小时用量上限。Max 则与 Pro 一样，保留五小时用量上限。

此次更名修正了一个连 Anthropic 自己也承认引发误解的名称，与此同时，一起集体诉讼正针对这些用量限制的宣传方式提出质疑。接下来值得关注的是取消限制的通知邮件发送得有多快、容量限制在实际使用中如何体现，以及集体诉讼的进展。
